prompt: In the equation $kx + 8 = 3x - 5$, $k$ is a constant. For which value of $k$ does the equation have **no** solution?
hint: No solution means the two sides never meet — parallel lines.

hints.text: No solution means the two sides never meet — parallel lines.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try the idea on plain numbers: $2x + 1 = 2x + 9$ has no solution, because subtracting $2x$ leaves $1 = 9$. Matching $x$-coefficients with different constants is exactly what makes an equation unsolvable.
If $k = 3$ the left side is $0$ and the equation reads $0 = -13$, which is impossible. So $k = 3$.

learningObjective: Determine the constant that makes a linear equation unsolvable.
explanation: Move everything to one side: $kx - 3x = -5 - 8$, so $(k - 3)x = -13$.
If $k \neq 3$ you can divide by $(k - 3)$ and get exactly one solution.
If $k = 3$, the equation becomes $0 \cdot x = -13$, or $0 = -13$ — false for every $x$. So there is no solution when $k = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Match the slopes
steps: Read each side as a line: $y = kx + 8$ and $y = 3x - 5$.
Two lines fail to intersect exactly when they are parallel — same slope, different intercept.
Same slope means $k = 3$; the intercepts $8$ and $-5$ already differ, so there is genuinely no solution.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Choice D, k = 8, is bait for matching the constant 8 instead of the coefficient of x.
Only the x-coefficients decide whether the sides can ever balance; the constants just decide between no solution and infinitely many once the coefficients match.
